football_evidence.question: Can Syracuse’s pass rush get to Kevin Jennings?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.2 points.
supporting: When SMU has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): SMU’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 19.6% of its runs, and Syracuse’s defense stops 24.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
In his last two games (Boston College and Virginia), Jennings averaged 6.2 yards per attempt, against 11.4 in his four games before that.
Syracuse comes in on 14 days of rest after an open week; SMU has had 7 days.
contradicting: When Syracuse has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Syracuse’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.4% of its dropbacks, and SMU’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Syracuse has the ball (the red zone): Syracuse’s offense succeeds on 33.6% of its red-zone plays, and SMU’s defense allows success on 30.3% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
When Syracuse has the ball (third down): Syracuse’s offense converts 40.2% of its third downs, and SMU’s defense allows opponents to convert 29.1% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).
When SMU has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): SMU’s offense averages 9.0 yards per pass attempt, and Syracuse’s defense allows 7.4 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
quarterbacks: Steve Angeli has completed 58 of 104 passes (55.8%) for 720 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in three games for Syracuse, and has been sacked on 8 of 112 dropbacks.
Malachi Nelson has completed 42 of 70 passes (60.0%) for 532 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in three games for Syracuse, and has been sacked on 5 of 75 dropbacks.
Kevin Jennings has completed 140 of 193 passes (72.5%) for 1,859 yards, 9.6 yards per attempt, 16 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for SMU, and has been sacked on 7 of 200 dropbacks.
